labels.label: bzprop:c3s4p6_facette_duale

hypotheses.paper: F une facette de W, a ∈ F

hypotheses.note: extended sense of § 1 l.289–290 (IsFacetteKExt: ∅ is the facette of dimension −1 when the noyau is empty); genuine facettes exactly when D(W_a) ≠ ∅

hypotheses.paper: qui ne dépend pas du choix de a
hypotheses.note: D(W_a) = D(W_b) for a, b ∈ F, one G for all a ∈ F, and G unique (∃!)

findings: Prop. 6 (l.1046–1049) is imprecise for the facettes of § 1 Déf. 4, which are nonempty: D(W_a) is empty whenever W_a = S(n), e.g. W = S(n), or W the closed quarter arc of S(1) and a its midpoint (F the open arc, D(W) = W ≠ ∅, D(W_a) = ∅): no facette of D(W) has closure ∅ (FacetteDualeInstance.prop6_needs_extended_facette). It holds in full when « facette » includes the facette ∅ of dimension −1 that l.289–290 introduces when the noyau is empty: D(W_a) = ∅ forces the noyau of D(W) to be empty (noyau_D_subset_D_coneAppui), and then 𝒟(F) = ∅ (prop6_facetteDuale). With genuine facettes it holds exactly when D(W_a) ≠ ∅ (prop6_facetteDuale_of_nonempty).

The proof's point a′ « intérieur au convexe D(W_a) muni de la topologie induite par celle de son support » exists only when D(W_a) ≠ ∅; it is formalized as an α(D(W_a))-least point (exists_alphaK_least) and 𝒟(F) is its facette (facetteDuale_eq_facetteK), as printed.
questions: Does « une facette de D(W) » in Prop. 6 include the facette ∅ of dimension −1 of l.289–290 (the dual facette of an « interior » facette F, e.g. the open facette of a convex body)? Reading taken: yes (IsFacetteKExt), which makes Prop. 6 true for every facette F; Prop. 8 (𝒟∘𝒟∘𝒟 = 𝒟, applied to every facette) seems to need it. Left unmarked pending the author's ruling.

labels.label: bzprop:c3s4p7_facette_duale_minimale

hypotheses.paper: F une facette de W, F′ une facette de D(W), ⟨F, F′⟩ = 0
hypotheses.note: IsFacetteK W F, IsFacetteK (D W) F′, OrthFacettes F F′; W convex

findings: No proof is printed (l.1062); proved: F′ ⊆ D(W_a), so D(W_a) ≠ ∅ and 𝒟(F) is the facette of an α-least point a′ of D(W_a), with a′ α(D(W)) p′ for every p′ ∈ F′. The hypothesis forces the nonempty case of Prop. 6, so Prop. 7 holds under either reading of « facette » there. The commentary l.1063–1066 is proved too: ⟨F, 𝒟(F)⟩ = 0 (orthFacettes_facetteDuale) and closure 𝒟(F) ⊇ F′ (subset_closure_facetteDuale).

instances: S(1), the closed quarter arc W = [a, b] (self-dual, D_arcS1): def4_instance (⟨{a}, {b}⟩ = 0, {a} a facette of W, {b} one of D(W)); facetteDuale_a0 (𝒟({a}) = {b}); prop6_needs_extended_facette (the open arc F: D(W_c) = ∅, 𝒟(F) = ∅).

S(2), the closed triangle T (simplexS (n+1) for every n; n = 1 is the triangle): D_simplexS (D(T) = T), facetteK_vertex0 / isFacetteK_vertex0 (a vertex is a facette), mk_mem_facetteK_oppVec (the opposite open edge {s(v) | v₀ = 0, vᵢ > 0} is a facette), facetteDuale_vertex0 (𝒟({s(e₀)}) = the opposite open edge, a facette of D(T), and ⟨{s(e₀)}, 𝒟({s(e₀)})⟩ = 0).
kb_proposals: Chapter3/FacetteDuale: a nonempty convex part C of S(n) has an α(C)-least point (exists_alphaK_least, from the strict exists_facette_support_eq on kPrime C; replace a least 0 by any nonzero point, which is α-below 0); its facette in any convex K ⊇ C has closure ⊇ C (subset_closure_facetteK, the path s((1−t)A′ + tB), t → 1⁻).

Points of f̄ ∩ K are α-below a facette f of K on S(n) (alphaK_of_mem_closure): the support supportK f is closed (isClosed_linearSubvariety_S) and the strict alphaK_iff_mem_supportK does the rest; this gives uniqueness of a facette with a given closure.

§ 4 Props. 4–7 on S(n) need only the duality inequality (prop2-style), never D′∘D = closure; and α of the positive orthant is « every coordinate vanishing at A vanishes at B » (alphaW_orthant_iff), a cheap source of facette computations on simplices.
Benzécri's 𝒟(F) needs the facette ∅ of dimension −1 (IsFacetteKExt, l.289–290) whenever D(W_a) = ∅; the dual of the interior facette of the quarter arc is ∅.
